prompt: A bus can hold less than $30$ riders. Write an inequality for the number $n$ of riders.
hint: Decide whether exactly $30$ riders is allowed. Read the wording "less than" carefully.

hints.text: Decide whether exactly $30$ riders is allowed. Read the wording "less than" carefully.
"Less than $30$" does not include $30$ itself, so use the strict symbol. Put $n$ on the left side.
The number of riders must stay below $30$, so the inequality is $n<30$.

explanation: The variable $n$ stands for the number of riders on the bus.
"Less than $30$" means $29$ or fewer, so $30$ is not allowed and the symbol is $<$.
Writing the variable first gives the inequality $n < 30$.
